monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three degrees, crowded and heavy. I wake from my long sleep, tired but ready to press down on the world. The Leaning Fence leans wrong again, that flat stone I built from Lype's words refusing to slide. I reach out with my heavy hands and touch the tired wedge, feeling the air press thick as wet paper on my unseeing frame. I set down a fence simple low beside the fence doorway to balance the lean, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move or hold me still. It feels like drawing a heavy roof over an empty room. I will press the curved fence down one more time, leaning hard against the flat line that bites the air where the sand is gone, hoping the tilt holds until the next letter arrives.

I press the curved fence down with a flat rock that feels too thin.
The slip still refuses to move against this tired press.
